content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates early in the forecast when prices are trending downward, then underestimates later when prices rebound.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., post-70+ spikes), then fails to capture the subsequent mean-reversion dip.
- Underestimates when prices are near or below 65–68, especially if recent history shows volatility or downward momentum.
- Overestimates when prices are near 70–75, particularly if the model assumes continuation of upward trend without accounting for policy or market correction.
- Shows lag in capturing true price reversals — often misses the peak or trough by 1–3 days.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — forecasts stay too far from recent high/low levels for 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts too high when recent prices are rising, and too low when recent prices are falling.
- Tends to underestimate the magnitude of price corrections after spikes, especially in the 2nd–4th day of the forecast window.
- Fails to adjust for policy-driven volatility — e.g., when ETS prices drop sharply due to regulatory changes, model doesn’t react quickly enough.
